title: Flowers, Pollination and Seeds
seo_title: Year 3 Science: Flowers, Pollination and Seeds Worksheets (Plant Life Cycle)
standard_text: Explore the part that flowers play in the life cycle of flowering plants, including pollination, seed formation and seed dispersal.
meta_desc: Free Year 3 science worksheets on flowers and the plant life cycle: pollination by insects and wind, seeds and fruits, and how seeds are dispersed. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Pollination, then seeds in a fruit, then dispersal.
body_html:
How to think about it

Flowers make seeds, and seeds grow into new plants.

  • Insects or the wind carry pollen from flower to flower: this is pollination.
  • After pollination, seeds form inside a fruit.
  • Seeds are spread (dispersed) by wind, water, animals or by bursting pods, then grow into new plants.
Example

What comes after pollination?

Pollen reaches the flower

Answer: seeds form inside a fruit

Example

Dandelion seeds travel how?

Fluffy parachutes

Answer: by the wind

Common mistakes

  • Thinking flowers are only for decoration.
  • Thinking fruits have nothing to do with seeds.
  • Thinking all seeds are spread by the wind.

faq.a: Flowers make seeds. Pollen from one flower reaches another, and then seeds form inside a fruit.
Pollination is moving pollen from one flower to another of the same kind. Insects such as bees and the wind do this.
Seeds are spread by the wind (dandelions, sycamores), by animals (blackberries, burdock), by water (coconuts) or by pods that burst open (peas).
